Give a movement model a preference for a habitat layer

habitat_selection.Rd

Attaches a habitat preference to a movement_model(), so that simulate_tracks() walks animals that select for, or against, the values of a raster layer with a known strength. The preference is a log weight per cell, beta * layer for a log-linear preference, or preference(layer) for any other shape, such as an optimum depth.

Usage

habitat_selection(model, layer, beta = NULL, preference = NULL)

Arguments

model

A movement_model() without a preference.

layer

A one-layer terra::SpatRaster of the habitat variable. At simulation it must have the geometry of the grid (terra::compareGeom()) and a finite value on every water cell. For bottom depth from a raster of negative depths, pass abs(lake) and name the layer, for example depth_m.

beta

One number: the log selection strength per unit of layer at the scale of one step. Negative values select low values of the layer. It is stored as given, so a fit to the tracks can be compared with it.

preference

A function of a vector of layer values that returns one finite log weight per value, for a preference that is not log-linear. Give exactly one of beta and preference.

Value

The movement_model, with an element selection (the layer, its name, beta and preference) and the source line extended. Tracks simulated with it carry a column heading and an attribute selection

that counts, per animal, the candidates drawn (proposals), the steps accepted (accepted), over_reach, above_bound and exhausted.

Details

The walker draws each moving step from the model without the preference: a step length and a turn, any goal pull on the bearing, and reflection at the shore. It accepts the step with probability w(end) / W, where w is the weight of the cell the step ends in and W the largest weight the step could reach from its start. A rejected step is drawn again from the same start and heading. This is rejection sampling, so the steps have exactly the density K(x, y) w(y) / integral of K w, where K is the walk without the preference. That density is the normalised product of a movement kernel and a habitat-selection function, Eqn 1 of Avgar et al. (2016). beta is therefore the step-scale selection coefficient that a conditional logit on the true steps estimates (see available_steps()).

W is the largest weight among the cells within the reach R of the start of the step, where R is the 0.9999 quantile of 100,000 step lengths from the model. A step longer than R, about 1 in 10,000, can end beyond those cells; it is accepted with probability min(1, w / W) and counted as over_reach. A step whose weight exceeds W is counted as above_bound. A step with 1,000 rejected candidates holds its position and is counted as exhausted. Each moving step therefore costs about 1 / acceptance candidates. On Stoney Lake with bottom depth, 20 animals walked for 48 hours from the same starts kept 0.51 of their candidates at beta = -0.3 per m and 0.39 at beta = 0.3. The script that gives these rates, https://github.com/jakebrownscombe/arraydesign/blob/main/validation/04_selection_acceptance.R, and its log in validation/outputs/ are in the repository and not in the installed package.

The weight is read at the cell that holds the end of the step, without interpolation, which is the value an analysis of the positions reads.

References

Avgar, T., Potts, J. R., Lewis, M. A. and Boyce, M. S. (2016). Integrated step selection analysis: bridging the gap between resource selection and animal movement. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 7, 619-630. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12528 (Eqn 1, p. 622: the density of the next position as the normalised product of a movement kernel and a habitat-selection function.)

See also

available_steps(), simulate_tracks()

Examples

lake <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif",
                                package = "arraydesign"))
depth <- abs(lake)
names(depth) <- "depth_m"
walk <- crw_model(30, 15, 40, time_step_s = 60)

# Select shallow water: log weight -0.3 per m of bottom depth
shallow <- habitat_selection(walk, depth, beta = -0.3)
shallow
#> <movement_model> 1 state 
#> time step: 60 s
#> selection: log weight -0.3 per unit of depth_m (rejection sampling)
#> source: crw_model(): gamma steps, mean 30 m and sd 15 m per 60 s; wrapped
#>   normal turns, sd 40 degrees; selection on depth_m: beta -0.3 per unit

# Three animals for 6 hours. The print counts candidates and accepted
# steps.
tracks <- simulate_tracks(lake, shallow, n_animals = 3, n_steps = 360,
                          seed = 1)
tracks
#> <sim_tracks> 3 animals, 1083 positions, time step 60 s
#> steps: 1080; as drawn 1035, reflected at the shore 45, held 0, still 0
#> selection: 1080 of 2194 candidates accepted (0.492); longer than the reach
#>   0, above the bound 0, exhausted 0
#>   path_id step                time        x       y cell state    heading
#> 1       1    0 2025-01-01 00:00:00 734954.0 4939591 4011     1         NA
#> 2       1    1 2025-01-01 00:01:00 734907.2 4939597 4011     1 -1.8743877
#> 3       1    2 2025-01-01 00:02:00 734924.5 4939567 4011     1 -3.2632172
#> 4       1    3 2025-01-01 00:03:00 734968.7 4939580 4011     1 -0.9015258
#> 5       1    4 2025-01-01 00:04:00 734977.8 4939578 4011     1  0.2728547
#> 6       1    5 2025-01-01 00:05:00 734999.8 4939614 4011     1 -0.1608713
attr(tracks, "selection")
#>   path_id proposals accepted over_reach above_bound exhausted
#> 1       1       941      360          0           0         0
#> 2       2       691      360          0           0         0
#> 3       3       562      360          0           0         0

# An optimum at 4 m bottom depth instead of a straight-line preference
habitat_selection(walk, depth,
                  preference = function(z) -0.1 * (z - 4)^2)
#> <movement_model> 1 state 
#> time step: 60 s
#> selection: log weight from a function of depth_m (rejection sampling)
#> source: crw_model(): gamma steps, mean 30 m and sd 15 m per 60 s; wrapped
#>   normal turns, sd 40 degrees; selection on depth_m: a log-preference
#>   function
